experiment.title: The flow keeps the partner's data when the partner's database is unreachable
experiment.description: The fault switch in the partner API (environment variable FAULT_DB) makes every call to its database hang for 10 s and fail, as a database that stopped answering would. k6 drives the fixed load profile through the coordinator and counts how many flow responses still carry the partner's record.

extensions.name: chaos-card
extensions.owner: partner, orders API on Google Cloud
extensions.steady_state: Measured with chaos/load.js and no fault: see the steady-state runs in the report. Every flow response carries the partner's record.
extensions.hypothesis: Given the load profile in chaos/slo.json, when the orders API's database is unreachable for 4 minutes, at least 99 % of GET /v2/items/:id still come back with partner.status = ok.

metric.name: share of GET /v2/items/:id with partner.status = ok
metric.observation_window: the 195 s of the probe that runs while the fault is active

extensions.injection: The partner's own fault switch: FAULT_DB=unreachable on its Cloud Run service, a new revision that makes each database call hang and fail.
extensions.blast_radius: Only the orders API's revision and its own database calls. The database server itself is untouched, and so is our cloud: the coordinator only sees slower or failed answers.
extensions.duration: about 4 minutes, from the switch to the rollback
abort_conditions: more than 50 % of the k6 requests failing (abortOnFail in chaos/load.js)
extensions.rollback: The rollback removes FAULT_DB, which deploys a clean revision. It always runs, even on abort.

steady-state-hypothesis.title: Under the fixed load, 99 % of the flow carries the partner's record
